intro: Professionals and everyday users convert watts (W) to horsepower (hp) (hp) when working across si and imperial standards in automotive engine output ratings, electric motor sizing, solar inverter specifications, and appliance load planning. One watt equals 0.001341 horsepower (hp), while 1 horsepower (mechanical) equals 745.699872 watts. Whether you are verifying power specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Exact NIST Factor vs. Early Rounding Drift
items: The exact conversion factor from Watt to Horsepower (Mechanical) is 0.00134102, derived from the 1959 International Yard and Pound Agreement (1 inch = 25.4 mm, 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg).

In structural engineering, CNC machining, or bulk inventory totals, rounding the multiplier to 2 decimal places too early can introduce cumulative tolerance errors; always compute with the full factor and round only the final displayed figure.

faqs.question: How many horsepower (hp) (hp) are in 1 watt (W)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.00134102 horsepower (hp) (hp) in 1 watt (W), which rounds to 0.0013 hp for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 horsepower (mechanical) equals 745.699872 watts.

faqs.question: How do I convert watts to horsepower (hp) (W to hp)?
faqs.answer: To convert watts to horsepower (hp), use the formula: hp = W × 0.00134102. For example, converting 1000 W gives 1.341 hp.

faqs.question: What is 1000 watts in horsepower (hp)?
faqs.answer: 1000 watts (W) equals exactly 1.341 horsepower (hp) (hp) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
